cards.text: Jesus tells His disciples a story: "There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions." That's like handing a friend your cookie box to hold and getting it back full of crumbs. So the rich man calls the manager in to ask, "What is this I hear about you?"

cards.question: The rich man calls his manager in and asks what this is he's hearing about him. Then what does he tell the manager?

answers.text: Turn in your account since you can't stay manager
Pay back every coin by tomorrow
Work for free until it's fixed

cards.text: The manager said to himself, "What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position?" He runs down his other options for work, and I bet he likes them about as much as I liked the back of the drawer behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: The manager tells himself he can always fall back on digging or begging once this job is gone.

cards.text: Then it clicks. He knows what he will do, and just like that he's got a plan for life after this job.

cards.question: The manager's plan is for people to welcome him into their ___ after his removal from management.

cards.text: So he calls in each one of his master's debtors, everybody who owes the boss. He starts with the first one: "How much do you owe my master?"

cards.question: The manager asks the first debtor how much he owes the master. What does the debtor say?

answers.text: A hundred measures of olive oil

cards.text: The manager tells him to take his bill, sit down QUICKLY and write a new number. Friend, I have never seen paperwork move that fast in my life.

cards.question: The first debtor owes a hundred measures of olive oil. The manager tells him to take his bill, sit down quickly and write ___.

cards.text: Then the manager asks another debtor, "And how much do you owe?" The man says he owes a hundred measures of wheat.

cards.question: The second debtor owes a hundred measures of wheat. The manager tells him to take his bill and write eighty.

cards.text: Now the master hears what his manager has done. Friend, I'm holding my breath like I'm watching a batch through the oven window.

cards.question: The master hears what the dishonest manager did with the debts. What does the master do?

answers.text: He commends him for acting shrewdly
He has him thrown into prison
He makes him pay back the difference

cards.text: Remember, the one who just got commended for acting shrewdly is the DISHONEST manager. Then comes a line that sizes up two groups side by side: the sons of this age and the sons of light.

cards.question: The line says the sons of light are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than the sons of this age.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves" and He doesn't pretend the money sticks around. Money's like a fresh cookie on my counter, baker, and it does NOT last.

cards.question: Jesus says to use worldly wealth to make friends. When that wealth is gone, what will those friends welcome you into?

cards.text: Jesus goes on, "Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much," and then He flips it around. Friend, I got my stamp right one crooked cookie at a time.

cards.question: Jesus says someone who is dishonest with very little can still be honest with much.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks a question about worldly wealth. The kind of question that follows you home and sits down on your couch.

cards.question: Jesus asks who will trust you with something greater if you haven't been faithful with worldly wealth. What is that greater thing?

cards.text: Then Jesus takes it one step further with another question, and this one is about belongings.

cards.question: Jesus asks: if you have not been faithful with the belongings of ___, who will give you belongings of your ___?

cards.text: Then Jesus lands it with a line about servants: "No servant can serve two masters." Friend, nobody shows up to the big game wearing BOTH teams' jerseys.

cards.question: Jesus says no servant can serve two masters. What does He say happens to a servant who tries?

answers.text: He'll hate one and love the other
He'll run out of time for both
He'll get paid by neither one

cards.question: Jesus says a person can serve both God and money, as long as they keep the two in balance.
